findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following locations are observed to have caulking that is cracking or has had the item pulled away from the wall enough to have a visible gap starting to form:
-The caulking of the mop sink.
-The caulking of the hand sink in the men’s bathroom.
Ensure these areas have the current caulking removed and replaced with new caulking to create a seal that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is observed bare wood on the shelving above the triple sink. Ensure this bare wood is sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking of the mop sink was observed to be in need of being resealed. Remove the old caulking and replace it with new to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-501.11: mPHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Still need test strips (have chlorine strips but purchased quaternary ammonium sanitizer).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: There are several toxic chemicals such as roach killer stored on the drainboards and shelf above the three compartment sink. Chemicals must be stored in a separate area that will not contaminate dishware.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11  (P) Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed bags of ice stored on the floor in the walk in freezer. Ice and all foods must be stored at least 6" off of the floor.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed the inside of the microwave to be soiled with food splatter and a couple areas that appear to be rusty. Clean microwave and consider replacing if it is rust as rust is not smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Replace microwave with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility does not have sanitizer or test strips available. Sanitizer and test strips are needed to wash, rinse and sanitize the coffee pots, soda nozzles, clean the counters, etc. Provide sanitizer and test strips. Plain unscneted bleach that has an EPA registration number and instructions for use on food contact surfaces would be sufficient. Prepare according to the label.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.
